newsitem.title: CANADA: Cameco to buy uranium from Russian weapons.
newsitem.headline: Cameco to buy uranium from Russian weapons.

text.p: Canadian mining company Cameco Corp said on Monday it has signed an agreement in principle to buy uranium removed from dismantled Russian nuclear weapons.

Cameco said it and two other companies, France's Cogema and U.S.-based Nukem Inc, will buy most of the natural uranium available from the dilution of weapons grade uranium to commercial grade uranium in Russia.
The agreement covers uranium available through 2006 to be delivered to the United States Enrichment Corp (USEC), Cameco said in a statement.
Cogema specializes in the nuclear fuel cycle and is 89-percent owned by the French government. Nukem is a privately-owned U.S. uranium trader.
The three companies will pay a discounted market price for the uranium and will guarantee minimum prices subject to certain conditions.
Each company will independently market their share of the uranium and will comply with USEC regulations, the statement said.
Cameco, Cogema and Nukem will advance to the Russian Federation Ministry of Atomic Energy (Minatom) up to one-half of each year's purchase price to a maximum of US$100 million against deliveries.
The uranium has become available following a 20-year agreement between the United States and Russia to dismantle nuclear weapons reached in 1993.

A majority of the resulting 400 million pounds of Russian U(3)0(8) (equivalent) will be sold for use in western nuclear power plants. The purchase agreement with Cameco, Cogema and Nukem is for at least 10 years, the statement said.
The agreement alleviates the market uncertainties surrounding the disposition of the uranium from dismantled weapons, said Bernard Michel, Cameco's chairman, president and chief executive officer.
"It provides Cameco, which will purchase some 45 percent of the available uranium, with a new and significant source of supply in addition to its own production," Michel said.
Cameco and other market players had accounted for this uranium in their long-term supply forecasts, but Michel said "until now, no one knew how it was going to be sold and by whom."
Cameco said it anticipated no change in either its production levels at existing operations or in its uranium mine development plans as a result of the acquisition of this material.
